title: ha/dr automation: multi-AZ failover + restore-drill runbooks-as-code + Helm/Terraform updates
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Add multi-AZ failover automation, runbooks-as-code for restore drills, Helm chart resiliency improvements, and Terraform module updates for private installer. No breaking API changes.
description:
Context:
Redwood Private installer needs repeatable, tested HA/DR automation for multi-AZ private deployments and on-prem installs. Customers running critical workloads expect documented runbooks that can be executed programmatically and run as part of scheduled restore drills. This PR bundles Helm chart hardening, Terraform module compatibility updates, and runbooks-as-code (playbooks) to automate failover and restore drills.

Summary of changes:
- Add runbooks-as-code under infra/playbooks/ha-dr with executable runbooks for: multi-AZ failover, cluster restore drill, and post-failover verification. Runbooks are simple YAML+script wrappers that the ops-runner can execute.
- Terraform updates to the private-installer module: expose az_count, fallback_zone priority list, and managed route53 failover record creation for control-plane endpoints.
- Helm chart improvements for redwood-operator and control-plane: anti-affinity, updated podDisruptionBudget (PDB), improved liveness/readiness probe timeouts, startup probes for db migrations, and tolerations for maintenance taints.
- Add upgrade/rollback helper scripts: infra/tools/upgrade-helper.sh and infra/tools/rollback-checker.sh to validate KV cache warmup and KV-consistency after modelserver upgrades.
- CI/workflow: add an integration CI job that runs a lightweight restore-drill smoke test using kind+localstack. The job is gated and allowed-failure on forks.

Motivation:
- Make DR playbooks repeatable and auditable (playbook history, parameters, and run timestamps).
- Ensure Helm charts are friendly to multi-AZ scheduling and safer during rolling upgrades.
- Let customers opt-in to automated DNS failover and fallbacks via Terraform module flags.

Checklist:
- [x] Runbooks authored and validated in staging against a 3-AZ topology
- [x] Terraform module unit tests updated and terraform fmt applied
- [x] Helm chart linted and smoke-deployed in CI
- [x] Integration CI job added (allowed failure on forks)
- [x] Documentation page updated: docs/private/ha-dr.md (opt-in guide and runbook reference)

Notes and links:
- Runbook definitions: infra/playbooks/ha-dr/*
- Terraform module: modules/private-installer
- Helm charts: charts/redwood-control-plane and charts/redwood-operator
- Linear: ENG-6421 (HA/DR runbooks), OPS-310 (restore drill automation)
- Jira: SUP-1982: customer incident that motivated automated restore drill templates

Operational implications:
- Default behavior is opt-out; Terraform variable enable_dns_failover=false by default.
- Running a restore drill will create temporary route53 failover records and cleanup on success/failure. Operators should review logs in infra/playbooks/runs/*.

How to review:
- Focus on infra/playbooks YAMLs and scripts for clarity and safe defaults
- Terraform changes are isolated to modules/private-installer and default values preserve existing behavior
- Helm changes are small, look at PDB and anti-affinity sections

Follow-ups (separate PRs):
- Add telemetry for runbook executions to the Console (ENG-6603)
- Expand restore drill CI job to run against a real cloud account in canary pipeline
